title: Power Stone 2
subtitle: A fight that falls out of the sky
summary: Four players compete for transforming stones while arenas collapse, move and carry the battle into new spaces.
body: Power Stone 2 is Capcom’s arena fighting sequel, first released for the NAOMI arcade system in April 2000, with a Japanese Dreamcast edition arriving that month. Up to four players can fight together, collecting Power Stones and using objects scattered around the stage. Returning adventurers are joined by new characters, while the larger group makes every loose gem and weapon a contested prize. The action remains easy to read through running, jumping, grabbing and throwing, but an encounter can now be interrupted by two more fighters.

A stage can change while the match continues. On the aircraft, the fight begins aboard a plane that eventually breaks apart, sending the players into a free-falling battle before they reach another platform. Movement therefore responds to the place coming apart as well as to the other fighters. Weapons and supplies emerge from item boxes, adding another reason to cross the arena. Collecting three Power Stones still brings a transformation, allowing a player who has escaped the crowd to return with a brief advantage.

The Dreamcast Adventure mode gives collected objects a life beyond an individual match. Items and money go into an inventory, and the shop allows purchases or combinations that can produce something new. Unlocking more objects broadens what may appear in later battles, connecting the short encounters to a longer collection. A VMU application also lets players inspect and exchange inventory information. These additions sit beside the changing arenas: one part of the sequel builds a catalogue of toys, while the other repeatedly finds new places to use them.
